action.action-desc: Mr. Harder of California introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Agriculture, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To expand access to integrated, community-driven health and nutrition services for underserved populations with high chronic disease prevalence, through coordinated local partnerships, measurable outcomes, and sustainable delivery models, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Partnerships for Better Health Act.

subsection.text: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the Secretary of Agriculture, shall establish a program under which the Secretary concerned will award grants to lead eligible entities to carry out activities that support integrated chronic disease prevention, management, and social support.
A lead eligible entity seeking a grant under this section shall submit an application at such time and in such manner, as the Secretary concerned may require. Such application shall include—

paragraph.text: a community needs assessment showing high chronic disease prevalence;
a care integration plan linking health and nutrition;
a measurable outcomes framework for each year of the grant; and
such other information as the Secretary concerned may require.

subsection.text: In awarding grants under this section, the Secretary concerned shall give priority to applicants serving communities (as determined by the Secretary concerned) that—

paragraph.text: have a high prevalence of chronic disease;
have high food insecurity;
are located in a health professional shortage area with a designation in effect under section 332 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254e);
are medically underserved communities (as defined in section 799B of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 295p));
are located in a rural area (as defined in section 1886(d)(2)(D) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395ww)); or
are located in an area of persistent poverty (as defined in section 6702 of title 49, United States Code).

subsection.text: A lead eligible entity that receives a grant under this section (and any member of a local coalition on whose behalf the application under this section is submitted) may use grant funds to—

paragraph.text: provide for integrated care delivery through—

subparagraph.text: the provision of care coordination across clinical, nutrition, and social services;
community health workers or patient navigators;
providing for referral systems between programs; or
transportation services;

paragraph.text: provide for nutrition and chronic disease education and self-management support through—

subparagraph.text: peer support and group education sessions; or

evidence-based, culturally and linguistically appropriate education materials delivered by a certified diabetes educator; community health worker, or trained peer educators using culturally appropriate printed and digital material;

paragraph.text: establish or expand a Food Is Medicine program;
establish or upgrade data infrastructure and conduct evaluations of outcomes, including through—

subparagraph.text: upgrades to data collection systems;
outcomes tracking;
coalition collaboration data; or
program evaluation and reporting; and

paragraph.text: carry out outreach and enrollment efforts, such as identifying eligible participants in services provided through such a grant and increasing community engagement and trust building with the community to be served by the lead eligible entity.

subsection.text: As a condition on the receipt of a grant under this section, the lead eligible entity shall agree—

paragraph.text: to exclusively use evidence-based or evidence informed models in providing services described in subsection (d);

to serve populations whose family income does not exceed 200 percent of the poverty line (as defined in section 673(2) of the Community Services Block Grant Act (42 U.S.C. 9902(2))) for a family of the size involved, or otherwise medically underserved; and
to ensure that each member of the local coalition involved—

subparagraph.text: maintains partnership agreements among the coalition for the duration of the period of the grant; and
participates in any Federal evaluations related to grants made under this section.

subsection.text: Funds made available under this section shall be used to supplement, and not supplant, non-Federal funds that would otherwise be used for activities authorized under this section.
The term of a grant awarded under this section shall not exceed 3 years. A grant may be renewed for an additional 2-year period, based on performance.

paragraph.text: Beginning not later than 6 months after the date on which a lead eligible entity receives a grant under this section, and every year thereafter, a lead eligible entity that receives a grant under this section shall submit to the Secretary concerned a report on—

subparagraph.text: the outcomes achieved by the program under this section; and
the progress made with respect to the design and implementation of the program.

paragraph.text: The report under subsection (a) shall include—

subparagraph.text: the demographics of participants in programs funded through the grant;
the services delivered by such programs;
the lessons learned from such programs and barriers to access to services provided by such programs; and
the health, social and access, and utilization outcomes of such programs specified in paragraph (3).

paragraph.text: The outcomes described in this paragraph are the following:

subparagraph.text: With respect to health outcomes, whether participants in programs funded through the grant had experienced a reduction in—

clause.text: HbA1c levels;
blood pressure; or
weight or body mass index (BMI).

subparagraph.text: With respect to social and access outcomes, whether such participants experienced—

clause.text: a change in food security status;
continuity of care;
increased engagement and retention in programs funded through the grant; or
a change in health behavior and dietary habits.

subparagraph.text: With respect to utilization outcomes, whether within the area served by the entity receiving the grant—

clause.text: had fewer emergency department visits related to chronic diseases; or
had fewer hospitalizations related to chronic diseases.

paragraph.text: The term Food is Medicine program means a structured intervention in which a healthcare provider prescribes or refers patients to receive, via home delivery, medically appropriate food, nutrition education, and related support as part of a treatment or prevention plan for diet-related disease.
The term lead eligible entity means the nonprofit or public entity submitting an application for a grant under this section on behalf of a local coalition, that—

subparagraph.text: has demonstrated—

clause.text: experience serving underserved or high-risk populations; and
capacity to manage Federal grant funds;

subparagraph.text: has in effect on the date on which the application is submitted, one or more formal agreements with a coalition partner; and
is one of the following:

clause.text: A Federally qualified health center (as defined in section 1861(aa) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395x(aa))).
A community health center receiving assistance under section 330 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254b).
A nonprofit hospital or health system.
A nonprofit organization with demonstrated healthcare expertise.
A food bank.
A nonprofit organization with demonstrated nutrition expertise.

paragraph.text: The term local coalition includes—

subparagraph.text: A clinical partner, such as—

clause.text: a Federally qualified health center or rural health clinic (as such terms are defined in section 1861(aa) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395x(aa)));
a community health center receiving assistance under section 330 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254b); or
a nonprofit hospital.

subparagraph.text: A food and nutrition partner, such as a food bank, food pantry network, or nonprofit food provider with capacity to source and deliver medically tailored or disease appropriate foods.
A public health or government partner, such as—

clause.text: a local or State public health department; or
Tribal health authority, where applicable.

subparagraph.text: A community-based organization, including—

clause.text: a faith-based organization;
a community action agency;
a social service nonprofit; and
an educational institution.

paragraph.text: The term Secretary concerned means—

subparagraph.text: the Secretary of Health and Human Services in the case of grants awarded to an entity specified in clauses (i) through (iv) of paragraph (2)(C); and
the Secretary of Agriculture in the case of grants awarded to an entity specified in clauses (v) and (vi) of paragraph (2)(C).

subsection.text: There are authorized to be appropriated $15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
